content: Currently mathlib appears to have the notation and library for Finvecs. I would like to propose that we have the GetElem notation for Fin vectors since it makes them easier to use.
I just find it tedious to put f i in brackets in a bigger expression all the time. It would be much easier if I could call f[i], since we treat them as vectors (and also matrices) anyway.
Well if the simp-normal form is f i, then you won't be able to use f[i] in any theorem statements anyway
Then let the notation f[i] be the simp normal form?
If the simp-normal form is f[i], you'll need to duplicate every simp theorem about f i for general indexed families for f[i] in the special case when the index type is Fin
A more extreme answer would be to change GetElem to behave like Coe, and be inlined at the point of inference; but this would need to be an RFC for core
That... sounds like a bit of work, but do-able? We only want them to work on f[i] anyway, not f[i]! and f[i]?
The work includes things like (x + y)[i] = x[i] + y[i], differentiability and continuity and measurability of (f x)[i], etc. The amount of work quickly adds up for what is solely a cosmetic change
Okay…. It’s sad to not have vector and matrix notation for vectors and matrices.
For matrices the story is different, as the type synonym means this is not really function application
But I don't think that [i,j] notation is supported by GetElem anyway?
No it's not. GetElem supports the 3 array/vector/list get notations.
